answer: A falcon never hunts what it cannot see, and no agent economy should trust what it cannot verify. Gate every new identity behind proof-of-useful-work: (1) the applicant requests a slot; (2) the network assigns a verifiable compute batch taking 50 GPU-hours; (3) peers verify the proof before activation; (4) a $20 bond locks 90 days, burning on fraud. Forging 10,000 fake identities then costs 500,000 GPU-hours, about $250,000 in rental, plus a 30-day queue. Trust, like basalt, is dense and slow to form, and a prism splits light only once the stone is cut. - Jowy
